Svitlana Kmit August 15, 2025 How to Relieve Pain in the Temporomandibular Joint Using Myofascial Release? Pain in the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is a frequent issue that impacts one’s quality of life. Chewing, talking, even smiling can cause discomfort. Accompanying symptoms – headache, tinnitus, neck pain – only worsen the problem.One of the most effective ways to relieve pain is myofascial release. This approach allows for the removal of deep muscle tension and improves blood circulation without the use of medications or surgical intervention. The temporomandibular joint is a complex structure that enables many of our usual actions: chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Any disruption in the system’s function can cause a range of unpleasant sensations, from discomfort to sharp pain. Understanding the causes is the first step towards effective therapy. Bruxism involuntary clenching or grinding of teeth during sleep or due to stress. Malocclusion or dysfunction of the masticatory apparatus. Stress and anxiety, which cause overstrain of the facial and neck muscles. Jaw injuries or past dental procedures. Posture disorders, especially in the cervical spine, which transmit tension to the TMJ. It is important to consider that jaw pain rarely occurs in isolation. It is often a symptom of deeper dysfunctions in the musculoskeletal or nervous system. Regular monitoring of habits (for example, clenching the jaw or chewing only on one side) helps to detect the problem in time. Proper diagnosis allows avoiding complications and chronic conditions. Career Path: Massage Therapist What Is Myofascial Release and How Does It Work? The muscles of our body are surrounded by fasciae (connective tissue sheaths), which form a single continuous system. When fasciae lose elasticity or become deformed, this leads to pain, limited mobility, and even joint dysfunction. Therefore, restoring their normal condition is the beginning of the path to reducing chronic tension. Myofascial release massage is a manual technique that affects the fasciae (which envelop the muscles) and promotes deep body relaxation.Principle of the method: The therapist “listens” to the patient’s body through palpation (a method of physical examination when the therapist feels tissue and organ changes with their hands). Identifies areas of increased fascial tension and maintains pressure on them for a few minutes. In response to such influence, fascia sliding improves, tissue tension decreases, and local blood and lymph flow normalize. This is not a massage in the usual sense. All actions are performed slowly, some sort of discomfort might be present during the release, with maximum attention to the body’s reactions.This approach is useful for working with delicate areas, especially in the jaw and neck region. Its effectiveness is confirmed in cases when other methods have not produced stable results. Regular sessions help reduce muscle tension, restore tissue mobility, and improve overall well-being. Muscles Associated With the Function of the TMJ The condition of the joint is closely connected with the muscles that provide its movement. Even slight overstrain of one of them can cause pain, asymmetry, or decreased jaw functionality.Key muscles affecting the joint: Masseter muscle – often prone to overstrain. Temporal muscle – works together with the masseter to elevate the jaw. Pterygoid muscles – responsible for the lateral movements of the jaw. Suprahyoid muscles and neck muscles – influence jaw stability and posture. The coordination of these muscles must be precise; otherwise, compensatory tension arises, which only worsens the situation. Often, patients do not realize that pain in the neck, face, or even shoulders may originate precisely from these structures. Therefore, working with the muscles is a mandatory stage in TMJ therapy. KMIT METHOD This is a modern myofascial release massage based techniques , developed by Svitlana Kmit in Chicago. It combines manual therapy and vacuum massage for deep work with the fasciae. The method is aimed at relaxing muscles, releases the fascia, improving blood and lymph flow, and eliminating chronic tension.“TMJ RELEASE” under the KMIT METHOD includes: Palpation of muscles to identify spasmed areas.Gentle, but deep pressure on the fasciae in the direction of tension.Gliding cupping therapy , as an add-on, to mobilize tissues. Focus on the masseter, temporal, and intraoral muscles (Buccal massage). The method does not require the application of forceful pressure, even though some sort of discomfort might be present during the actual release. Its foundation is based on respect for the natural biomechanics of the body.This approach not only reduces pain, but also promotes better body awareness. Clients often notice overall relaxation, lightness in the jaw and face after the first session. The KMIT METHOD is effective both: as a standalone therapy and in combination with home exercises to achieve lasting results. How “TMJ RELEASE” Helps With TMJ Pain? Pain in the temporomandibular joint often has not only a local, but also a systemic origin. The KMIT METHOD takes this into account and works with the body comprehensively.Thanks to precise and deep influence, it is an effective solution for: Chronic jaw pain: reducing pressure on the TMJ by relaxing the masseter and temporal muscles. Clicking and limited jaw movement: improving fascia mobility and reducing friction in the joint. Tension headaches and ear pain: eliminating muscle spasms. Muscle imbalance: correcting facial asymmetry. A distinctive feature of the method is working not only with external, but also internal structures, allowing effects to be felt after the first session. KMIT METHOD based services also affects the nervous system state — promoting overall calming, which is important in chronic pain. Many patients report reduced anxiety and improved sleep. This holistic approach makes the method so effective in TMJ dysfunction therapy. Advantages of the KMIT Method Modern approaches to treating painful symptoms increasingly favor gentle, deeply therapeutic techniques. The KMIT METHOD is one of the non-medicated ways to influence musculo-fascial dysfunctions, especially in the jaw area.Its advantages: Safety: the technique does not cause pain and is suitable even for sensitive patients. Depth of influence: KMIT METHOD works not only with muscles, but also with fasciae and the nervous system. Complexity: the method considers not only the local pain area but also the overall body condition. Lasting effect: results are consolidated for a long time due to the harmonization of bodily structures. Individual approach: therapy is adapted to the needs of the specific person and their problem. Besides physical changes, the method helps to feel bodily balance and emotional relief. It does not require long recovery or additional procedures. That is why KMIT METHOD is suitable for people, looking for a natural, and effective way to reduce TMJ pain. Massage Classes Start Soon! Start Your New Career Today! When to See a Myofascial Release Specialist? Persistent TMJ pain, headaches, and jaw clicking. A feeling of stiffness or limitation when opening the mouth. Stress symptoms: facial muscle tension, bruxism. Previous injuries or dental procedures. Chronic tension in the neck, shoulders, back. If symptoms do not disappear after 7–10 days, do not delay the consultation. Self-massage and home exercises can be helpful; however, the best results are achieved by combining these methods with individually tailored therapy under the supervision of an experienced specialist. Pain in the temporomandibular joint often has a myofascial origin. Thanks to its delicacy, precision, and depth, the KMIT METHOD not only relieves pain, but also changes the quality of life.Listen to your body’s signals and allow yourself to experience comfort and balance — free from pain, stress, and tension.
